NATIONAL ASSEMBLY RULES FOR THE ENFORCEMENT OF THE ACT ON THE REPORT AND DISCLOSURE OF MILITARY SERVICE RECORDS OF PUBLIC SERVANTS

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of these National Assembly Rules is to prescribe matters delegated by the Act on the Report and Disclosure of Military Service Records of Public Servants (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") and matters necessary for its enforcement.

Article 2 (Reporting of Military Service Records)
(1) Candidates for public office (hereinafter referred to as "candidates") required to report military service records pursuant to Article 10 (1) of the Act (Reporting and Disclosure of Military Service Records of Candidates for Public Office Requiring the National Assembly's Consent to Appointment, etc.) shall be as follows:
1. Prime Minister;
2. Chairperson of the Board of Audit and Inspection;
3. Chief Justice of the Supreme Court and Justices of the Supreme Court;
4. President of the Constitutional Court and three Justices of the Constitutional Court elected by the National Assembly;
5. Three members of the National Election Commission elected by the National Assembly;
6. Secretary General of the National Assembly;
7. Other candidates whose appointment requires the consent of the National Assembly or who are elected by the National Assembly under any Act.
(2) A candidate under paragraph (1) shall enter the military service records prescribed in Article 3 of the Act (Persons Subject to Reporting and Military Service Records to Be Reported) in the Report on Military Service Records of a Candidate for Public Office in attached Form 1 (hereinafter referred to as a "report") and submit the report to the Speaker of the National Assembly. In the case of a candidate requiring the consent of the National Assembly, the appointing authority shall attach the report to the motion for consent to appointment and submit it; in the case of a candidate elected by the National Assembly, the candidate shall submit it directly.
(3) The Speaker of the National Assembly shall check whether the report submitted under paragraph (2) lacks any required attached documents or contains any error in its entries or other such deficiencies, have necessary corrections or supplements made, and issue to the candidate a Receipt of Report on Military Service Records of a Candidate for Public Office in attached Form 2.

Article 3 (Disclosure of Military Service Records)
The Speaker of the National Assembly shall publish and disclose in the National Assembly Bulletin the military service records of a candidate for public office in attached Form 3, on the basis of military service records reported pursuant to Article 10 (1) of the Act.

Article 4 (Verification of Reported Military Service Records)
In any of the following cases, the Speaker of the National Assembly may directly verify the contents of the military service records reported by a candidate or request the Commissioner of the Military Manpower Administration to verify them:
1. Where the Speaker of the National Assembly deems verification necessary;
2. Where a Member of the National Assembly raises a written objection alleging omission or a false report in the candidate's reported military service records, accompanied by supporting evidence.

Article 5 (Handling of Verification Results)
Where an omission or false statement is verified in the military service records reported by a candidate, the Speaker of the National Assembly shall prepare the Verification Results concerning Military Service Records of the Candidate for Public Office in attached Form 4 and publish and disclose them in the National Assembly Bulletin.

ADDENDUM <National Assembly Regulation No. 105, 1999.9.30>

These Rules shall enter into force on the date of their adoption by the National Assembly.

INSTRUCTIONS FOR COMPLETING MILITARY SERVICE RECORDS OF THE CANDIDATE AND LINEAL DESCENDANTS

① In the "Category" field, enter "Consent to Appointment" or "Election".
② In the "Prospective Position" field, enter the position for which the candidate is proposed for consent to appointment or election.
③ In the "Name" field, write the candidate's name in Hangul.
④ In the "Relationship to Candidate" field, distinguish the candidate from his or her lineal descendants, and list the lineal descendants in birth order, including descendants who will have reached 18 years of age as of one month before the date on which the motion for consent to appointment or election is submitted. However, women who are not liable for military service and men under 18 years of age are excluded.

"Instructions for entries"
1. Classify persons as the candidate, son, grandson or maternal grandson.
2. For sons, specify "eldest son", "second son", "third son", etc.
3. For grandchildren, enter only "grandson" or "maternal grandson".

⑤ In the "Name" field, write the reportable person's name in Hangul and enter the Chinese characters in parentheses.
⑥ through ⑧: Omitted.
⑨ In the "Military Service Records" field, reproduce the military service particulars exactly as shown on the certificate of military service record issued by the head of the regional military manpower office.
⑩ In the "Remarks" field:
- If the candidate herself is a woman, enter "Woman".
- Where a lineal descendant of the candidate requests that the name of a disease or details of a physical or mental disability not be disclosed pursuant to Article 14 (2) of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Report and Disclosure of Military Service Records of Public Servants, enter "Request for Non-Disclosure of Disease Name (Details of Physical or Mental Disability)", and the candidate or the person concerned shall affix a seal or sign.
